newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. rescinds approvals for three El Al routes.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rescinds approvals for three El Al routes.

text.p: The United States has informed Israel and state airline El Al that it rescinded approval for three El Al routes between U.S. cities and Tel Aviv, Israeli aviation officials said on Thursday.

The action was taken in response to a decision by Israeli authorities not to approve a New York-Athens-Tel Aviv route by U.S.-based Tower Air starting this summer, El Al spokesman Nahman Klieman told Reuters.
He said Israel had rejected the application because it had not been filed on time and told Tower it could begin the flights in October.
"We were surprised by the American decision. The transport minister will meet with the U.S. ambassador next week and we hope we can find a solution," said Transport Ministry spokesman Avner Ovadiah.

The El Al routes include a twice weekly flight running from Baltimore-Washington, a weekly flight to Orlando, Florida, which was due to operate during the summer; and a route from Dallas-Fort Worth, Klieman said.
El Al had received permission to operate the Dallas-Fort Worth route but had not scheduled any flights, Klieman said.
Klieman said El Al hoped the United States would re-authorise the routes once Tower's route had been cleared. "We will have to apply again and see what happens," he said.
Klieman said the routes were to carry 450 passengers a week and the airline would instead operate connecting flights on North American Airlines between those cities and New York.
"We would have preferred to operate the flights as non-stop, but we will honour our obligations to our passengers...to fly them to Tel Aviv as originally planned," he said.
